# Concrete maturity calculator

> Free, open-source concrete maturity calculator: reads a temperature logger's CSV and the lab breaks for a mix, fits the strength-maturity curve (logarithmic, hyperbolic or exponential), and estimates each sensor's in-place strength and when it reaches a target, by Nurse-Saul or equivalent age (the maturity method described in ASTM C1074). Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates, not engineering advice; confirm with field-cured specimens or other in-place tests before stripping forms or post-tensioning.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/concrete-maturity/)
- [The maturity method explained, with a worked example](https://marisstella.app/concrete-maturity/maturity-method-explained.html)

## Inputs

- Logger CSV: a date/time or elapsed-time column and one column per sensor (°C or °F). Elapsed headers may name hours, minutes, seconds or days (`Elapsed (min)`, `elapsed_min`, `Age (days)`); impossible timestamps such as 30 February are rejected, not rolled over.
- Lab breaks: one specimen per line, "age_days, strength" (moist-cured at a stated temperature) or "maturity, strength".
- Target strength; optional assumed future temperature.
- Mix calibration (optional): mortar cubes at three or more curing temperatures, one per line "temperature, age_hours, strength", plus "set, temperature, hours" lines for final setting time. Returns each temperature's rate constant k, the mix's datum temperature (k against T) and activation energy (ln k against 1/T), and how tightly all cubes fall on one strength-maturity curve under the default, fitted and best-single-curve values. CLI: `node cli.mjs --calibrate cubes.txt`.

## Source

- [Source code, CLI and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/concrete-maturity): FSL-1.1-MIT licensed. `node cli.mjs logger.csv --cal breaks.txt --target 3000`.
